clue.text: Take note of advice to artesian surveyor

definitions.meaning: to pay close attention to something
someone surveying for an artesian well might be told to mark the well's site

explanation.definitionFit: To mark something well is to heed it carefully; read literally, the phrase tells a well-digger to put a marker on the spot.

clue.text: It is anything but sleek in form and over weight

definitions.text: It is anything but sleek in form and over weight

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second
sleek put into a new form means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Something described as far from sleek, misshapen and too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' rearranges SLEEK to SKELE, which sits 'over' TON in this down entry. The whole clue is a teasing description: a bony frame is anything but sleek.
explanation.definitionFit: A bony frame is the opposite of sleek flesh, so the whole clue describes it ironically.

clue.text: Homicide squad's first question of whomsover happens to be around

definitions.meaning: murder detectives would first ask whether there is a corpse, a 'body', anywhere
whoever at all is present, any person

explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means any person at all, and split in two it is the detectives' query about a corpse.

clue.text: Plural nouns and singular verbs used ceremonial parades

definitions.meaning: plural nouns and third-person singular verbs typically end in the letter S
blades carried at military ceremonies

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as S + WORDS: words ending in S, like plural nouns and 'he walks'. The clue as held appears to lack 'at' before 'ceremonial'.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers carry blades at ceremonial parades, and the split form describes words ending in the letter S.

clue.text: Italian has to enlist with non-commissioned men

parts.note: to enlist is to sign up for service
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An Italian man joins up alongside the rank-and-file soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Signor is the Italian title for a gentleman, so it can stand for an Italian man.

clue.text: Apartheid issue in which written evidence is put down

definitions.meaning: apartheid was about the divide between races described by skin colour

definitions.text: in which written evidence is put down
definitions.meaning: something set down in writing, in ink on paper

explanation.definitionFit: The racial divide of apartheid was framed as a colour question, and the idiom also means set down in writing.

clue.text: Installing wooden walls and floors for temporary accommodation

definitions.meaning: fitting planks to a home: putting boarding on a house
lodgings where guests pay for a room and meals

explanation.definitionFit: A lodging establishment for paying guests; read literally the phrase describes covering a house with planks.

clue.text: Household word for the privileged classes

definitions.meaning: an archaic sense: a domestic setup or household
the ruling elite who hold power in society

explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant a domestic household and now names the powerful elite who run a society.

clue.text: John takes Albert to be a menialdog

parts.note: Jack is a familiar form of the name John
Al is a short form of Albert

explanation.surface: A man named John recruits Albert to be his drudge.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held runs 'menial' and 'dog' together; both are senses of the answer: a drudge doing another's dirty work, and a wild canine.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild canine scavenger, and by extension a lackey who does menial tasks for someone else.

clue.text: One enters a London hospital for titled people

indicators.note: one piece enters, goes inside, the other

parts.note: Barts is St Bartholomew's, a famous London hospital
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient is admitted to a London hospital reserved for aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: BARTS is the familiar name for St Bartholomew's Hospital in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronets hold a hereditary title below baron, so they are titled people.

clue.text: I travel to the East

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
to go is to travel

explanation.definitionFit: The self, the 'I' of psychology, is the ego in Latin and Freudian terms.

clue.text: Refer to a classified item

definitions.meaning: to mention or allude to something
a small advertisement in the classified columns

explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is to mention it; the noun is a short form of advertisement, such as a classified ad.

clue.text: Give an account of two consecutive notes by an old writer

parts.note: D and E are neighbouring notes in the musical scale
a scribe was a copyist of manuscripts in former times

explanation.surface: A musician recounts a story using two notes and an ancient copyist.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account of something is to depict it in words.

clue.text: A cry from the crow's nest

definitions.text: A cry from the crow's nest

parts.words: A cry from the crow's nest
parts.note: the crow's nest suggests a lookout on a ship shouting, but here it is a crow calling from its own nest

explanation.definitionFit: The harsh call a crow makes is its characteristic cry.

clue.text: Have a tendency to lean

definitions.meaning: to be disposed towards something
to slope or tilt

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to be disposed towards something, and also to slope or tilt.

clue.text: A personal promise apparently taken amiss

definitions.meaning: with an apostrophe the letters say 'I will', a promise in the first person
badly or wrongly, as in to take something badly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken amiss' and 'taken ill' mean the same thing: offence was taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means badly or wrongly, and with an apostrophe the letters become the first-person pledge 'I will'.

clue.text: Case for formal court dress

definitions.meaning: a legal action brought before a court
split in two, an outfit worn for legal proceedings

explanation.definitionFit: A legal case is a civil action in court; split, it suggests the clothing a lawyer wears.

clue.text: Dog Latin as a degenerative form

indicators.note: a degenerated form of the words is a corrupted rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Dog Latin, the mock language, described as a debased version of real Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog Latin' is a real phrase for bad Latin, which makes 'Dog' look like part of a phrase rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian is a breed of dog, also called the German shepherd.

clue.text: Hard to believe gin is employed for soaking

parts.note: steep is informal for excessive or unreasonable, a claim hard to accept

indicators.note: gin put to work is reworked, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An unlikely tale that gin is used to soak something.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeping is leaving something immersed in liquid, as tea leaves are.

clue.text: Doodlebug is an example to a sluggard and a beastly king

parts.note: Proverbs says 'Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways'
the lion is called king of the beasts

explanation.surface: Something presented as a moral example to the lazy and a royal animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodlebug is the American name for the larva of this insect, which digs pit traps.

clue.text: No milk and sugar for the war minister!

definitions.text: No milk and sugar for the war minister!

parts.words: No milk and sugar for the war minister!
parts.note: tea without additions is plain cha, CHA being slang for tea; the war minister is an army clergyman

explanation.surface: A government war minister is denied milk and sugar in his tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'war minister' suggests a government post, but means a minister of religion serving the armed forces; CHA is slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An army padre is a minister of religion who serves troops in wartime.

clue.text: Boat which should be securely tied up

definitions.meaning: a mail boat on a regular route

definitions.text: which should be securely tied up
definitions.meaning: a parcel, which should be firmly bound before posting

explanation.definitionFit: A packet boat carried mail on a regular route; a parcel is tied up securely for posting.

clue.text: Clever design of statue

indicators.note: a new design of the word means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for the clever design of a sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and quick-witted are synonyms here.

clue.text: Look at the boil

parts.note: to see is to look at

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect a boil, the skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boil' reads as a noun, an abscess, but the definition is the verb: to bubble or rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that is bubbling furiously, or a person who is fuming with anger, is said to boil.

clue.text: Liquid meal

definitions.meaning: a drink brewed from leaves
a light afternoon or evening meal

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a drink brewed from leaves and, in Britain, a light afternoon or evening meal.

clue.text: Oman port and the Spanish wine from France

parts.note: Muscat is the capital and port of Oman
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Wine shipped through an Omani port and Spain, though actually French.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscatel is a sweet wine made from muscat grapes, produced in southern France among other places.

clue.text: One who is generous in giving advice

definitions.meaning: someone who leaves generous gratuities
someone who passes on hints and pointers

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves gratuities, and a punning sense of one who passes on useful hints.

clue.text: It provides current attraction at the science exhibition

definitions.text: It provides current attraction at the science exhibition

parts.words: It provides current attraction at the science exhibition
parts.note: current suggests a popular present-day draw, but here means electric current producing magnetic pull

explanation.definitionFit: A coil carrying electric current becomes magnetic, attracting iron, so current gives it its attraction.
